title: change tracking identity resolution no tracking and concurrency tokens
concepts: A DbContext state manager tracks entity identity and values so SaveChanges can calculate database changes. Change detection can use snapshots, notifications, or proxies depending on configuration.

Tracking queries perform identity resolution: a key already present in the context maps to the same object instance. No-tracking queries avoid state-manager work; the identity-resolving no-tracking variant maintains identity only for that query.
Entity state describes the intended persistence action, but attaching or updating a disconnected graph requires deliberate key and property-state decisions to avoid unintended writes.

Optimistic concurrency adds a token to the update predicate. If another writer changed the row, SaveChanges throws DbUpdateConcurrencyException; the application must decide whether to reload, merge, retry, or reject.
A DbContext cannot be used for concurrent operations. Keep its lifetime bounded and await database work before reusing it.
